articles.title: Gradient Spectra→Void
articles.summary: Rainbow spiral pinwheel of red, orange, cyan and blue, fading out to black at the edges. Reads as a rainbow heat-map fade, hot orange at the base to dark navy up top, with a scratchy net that gives it a hairy, neon-wire look.
articles.what: Vivid spectraflame color fading radially into total vantablack void — light to nothing Up close: Vertical colour sweep, orange at the bottom through yellow-green, teal and cyan to deep blue-navy at the top, covered by a tangle of thin straight scratch lines, 60-150 px long, in red, yellow and cyan that cross at random. From a distance: Reads as a rainbow heat-map fade, hot orange at the base to dark navy up top, with a scratchy net that gives it a hairy, neon-wire look. Measured spec (average): metal 117, roughness 117, coat 123. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: hero panel, hood, roof.
Fits: show car, open wheel, gt / sports car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Gradient Spectra→Void" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Side panels and doors: bottom orange at the rocker, navy at the roofline
Hood and rear quarter also work; fade is vertical so orient with the body height
Hard to read over the lines; white numbers on the blue top can work with a thick outline.
None: the sweep plus scratches is the design
Pairs well with: black, chrome, white.
pitfalls: Not a spiral pinwheel fading to black: the old card is wrong; the render is a vertical rainbow fade with random scratch lines
Not fully dark: the top is deep blue, not vantablack
Avoid: small numbers over the busy centre, next to other loud gradients.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 117 (pearl-level metal), roughness 117 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 123 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the busy centre, next to other loud gradients.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none: the sweep plus scratches is the design; bold black stripes: contrast on the colour
Patterns to avoid: lines, hair, scratch or flame patterns: tangle with the scratches; dots, camo: noise on noise
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sweep: deeper candy feel; none for metal: already medium
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

examples.title: Put it on a zone
